verdict: CrowdStrike grew revenue 26% to $1.47B with record new subscription deals, yet GAAP profit was just $5M — heavy spending and stock pay ate the quarter, and interest earned on its cash pile covered a small operating loss.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: The Falcon security platform, sold by subscription — 95% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Security experts for hire — incident response and setup help.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling Falcon to enterprises — the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the Falcon platform and its AI defenses.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Record new business
takeaways.text: Net new ARR — new subscription value signed in the quarter — hit a record $333M, up 51%, taking total ARR to $5.84B. AI-driven attacks are pushing companies to consolidate security onto Falcon.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit is a rounding error
takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $5M on $1.47B of revenue. Excluding stock-based pay, profit was $323M — the gap is shares handed to employees, a real cost that simply doesn't use cash.

takeaways.title: Cash flow tells another story
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was a Q2 record $377M — customers pay subscriptions upfront, so cash arrives long before the revenue is counted.

oneTimers: The core business ran at a $33M operating loss; interest earned on the company's $5.0B cash pile more than covered it, leaving the small $5M profit. A $1M tax benefit (the tax line added money back) helped too.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$37M: $44M of interest earned on CrowdStrike's $5.0B cash pile, minus $6M of interest expense and $1M of other costs.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
